segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, the dwelling of God is with humanity, and he will dwell with them, and they will be his peoples, and God himself will be with them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and he will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death will be no more; neither mourning nor crying nor pain will be any more. The first things have passed away.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the one seated on the throne said,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “Look, I am making all things new.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “Write this, for these words are faithful and true.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to me,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “They have come to pass. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. To the one who is thirsty I will give from the spring of the water of life, free of charge.

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: The one who conquers will inherit these things, and I will be his God and he will be my son.

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: But as for the cowardly and faithless and detestable, and murderers and the sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars, their share is in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur, which is the second death.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues came and spoke with me, saying,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great, high mountain and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: having the glory of God. Its radiance was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It had a great, high wall; it had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names inscribed on them, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: on the east three gates, and on the north three gates, and on the south three gates, and on the west three gates.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The one who was speaking with me had a golden measuring rod to measure the city and its gates and its wall.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The city is laid out as a square, its length the same as its width. And he measured the city with the rod: twelve thousand stadia. Its length and width and height are equal.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He also measured its wall: one hundred forty-four cubits by human measure, which is also the angel’s.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The material of its wall was jasper, and the city was pure gold, like pure glass.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The foundations of the city wall were adorned with every kind of precious stone. The first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, the twelfth amethyst.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the twelve gates were twelve pearls; each one of the gates was made from a single pearl. And the main street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God, the Almighty, is its temple, and the Lamb.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the city has no need of the sun or of the moon to shine on it, for the glory of God has illuminated it, and its lamp is the Lamb.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The nations will walk by its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory into it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Its gates will never be shut by day, for there will be no night there,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they will bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But nothing unclean will ever enter it, nor anyone who does what is detestable or deals in lies, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s book of life.

notes.note: In the Scriptures and in Revelation itself the sea stands for chaos and threat; the beast rises from it (13:1) and it holds the dead (20:13). Its absence signals the removal of everything hostile to God's order, not a remark about geography.

The Greek word means a tent and is the Septuagint's term for the tabernacle, the tent-sanctuary where God was present with Israel in the wilderness. The verb “dwell” that follows comes from the same root, and the English keeps that echo. The promise takes up Leviticus 26:11–12 and Ezekiel 37:27.

notes.phrase: they will be his peoples, and God himself will be with them
notes.traditional: they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God
notes.note: Manuscripts are divided between the plural “peoples” and the singular “people”; the plural, followed here, widens the old covenant formula for Israel to many peoples. Many manuscripts also add “as their God” (or “and be their God”) at the end of the verse; the Greek text translated here does not include it.

The Greek verb is plural, literally “they have happened,” and most likely refers to the words just declared faithful and true, or to the “all things” being made new. Most translations give the singular “It is done,” matching the similar cry at 16:17, where the Greek is in fact singular.

notes.phrase: I will be his God and he will be my son
notes.note: This echoes God's promise about David's heir in 2 Samuel 7:14, “I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me.” The royal promise is here extended to everyone who conquers, male or female. The singular “son” is kept so that the allusion stays audible.

The word can mean either “unbelieving” or “unfaithful, untrustworthy.” Following “cowardly,” and in a book addressed to churches under pressure to give way, it probably points to failure of loyalty rather than simply to outsiders who do not believe. Many translations nevertheless have “unbelieving.”

The Greek has no article and could also be read “in spirit,” describing a visionary state rather than naming God's Spirit. The same phrase occurs at 1:10, 4:2 and 17:3. The language recalls Ezekiel 40:2, where the prophet is taken in visions to a very high mountain to see the restored city.

A stadion was roughly 185 metres, so the figure comes to about 2,200 kilometres (some 1,400 miles) in each dimension. The number is kept as written because it is symbolic, twelve times a thousand, matching the twelves that run through the chapter. A city of equal length, width and height recalls the cube-shaped inner sanctuary of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:20).

notes.phrase: one hundred forty-four cubits by human measure, which is also the angel’s
notes.note: A cubit was about 45 centimetres, so the wall measures roughly 65 metres; the number is twelve times twelve. The text does not say whether this is the wall's height or its thickness, and interpreters are divided. The closing phrase seems to mean that the angel is using ordinary human units, though its exact sense is disputed.

Ancient gem names do not map neatly onto modern mineralogy, and the identification of several stones in this list is uncertain. The stone called “sapphire,” for example, was probably lapis lazuli, and “jasper” covered a wider range of stones than it does today. The list resembles the stones on the high priest's breastpiece (Exodus 28:17–20), though the two do not correspond exactly.
The word means a broad street and can also denote an open square or plaza. It is singular here, and could be meant collectively for the city's streets in general.

This is the same Greek word that elsewhere in the New Testament is translated “Gentiles,” meaning the non-Jewish peoples. Here, where the peoples of the whole world are in view, it is rendered “nations.” The picture draws on Isaiah 60, where nations and kings come to Jerusalem's light bringing their wealth.

candidates.reason: The recurring ‘one who conquers/overcomes/is victorious’ formula in Revelation 2–3 and 21, and in John and 1 John, needs one English verb so that readers can hear the refrain.

The verb and its noun σκηνή (tent/tabernacle/dwelling) occur in John 1:14, Hebrews and Revelation, and translators vary between ‘dwell’, ‘tabernacle’ and ‘pitch a tent’, obscuring the tabernacle allusion.
ναός (the sanctuary building) and ἱερόν (the temple complex) are both commonly rendered ‘temple’; a decision is needed on whether to distinguish them consistently.
The πορν- word group recurs across Paul, Hebrews and Revelation, with renderings ranging from ‘fornicator’ to ‘sexually immoral’ to ‘one who uses prostitutes’.
The word and its cognate verb (v. 8) recur in the Gospels and Revelation, including ‘abomination of desolation’, and translators vary between ‘abomination’ and ‘detestable thing’.
